title: Bianisotropic Space-Time Metasurfaces
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate bianisotropic space-time metasurfaces based on varactor-loaded omega-shaped meta-atoms. Full-wave simulations reveal coexisting electric and ring-associated magnetic responses at the operating frequency, while a traveling-wave modulation drives reactive loads embedded in both responsive regions of the meta-atom. The resulting space-time modulation generates a reconfigurable polychromatic spectrum with directional sideband radiation governed by Floquet phase matching. Under free-space illumination, the same metasurface preferentially couples the received field toward one guided port, producing modulation-controlled directional routing. The measurements characterize the collective bianisotropic response rather than independently retrieving its electric, magnetic, and magnetoelectric susceptibility components. These results establish bianisotropic space-time metasurfaces as a platform for jointly controlling frequency generation, directional radiation, and wave routing within a single dynamically modulated aperture.
